\textbf{1} Express the following as trigonometric ratios of either $30^\circ$, $45^\circ$ or $60^\circ$, and hence find their exact values.\quad
\textbf{a } $\sin135^\circ$\quad\textbf{b } $\sin(-60^\circ)$\quad\textbf{c } $\sin330^\circ$\quad\textbf{d } $\sin420^\circ$\quad\textbf{e } $\sin(-300^\circ)$\quad\textbf{f } $\cos120^\circ$\quad\textbf{g } $\cos300^\circ$\quad\textbf{h } $\cos225^\circ$\quad\textbf{i } $\cos(-210^\circ)$\quad\textbf{j } $\cos495^\circ$\quad\textbf{k } $\tan135^\circ$\quad\textbf{l } $\tan(-225^\circ)$\quad\textbf{m } $\tan210^\circ$\quad\textbf{n } $\tan300^\circ$\quad\textbf{o } $\tan(-120^\circ)$.
transcription.notes: Exact text and mathematics visually checked against original asset.

transcription.tex:
\textbf{a } $\sin135^\circ=+\sin45^\circ$ ($135^\circ$ is in the second quadrant at $45^\circ$ to the horizontal.) So $\sin135^\circ=\frac{\sqrt2}2$.
\textbf{b } $\sin(-60^\circ)=-\sin60^\circ$ ($-60^\circ$ is in the fourth quadrant at $60^\circ$ to the horizontal.) So $\sin(-60^\circ)=-\frac{\sqrt3}2$.
\textbf{c } $\sin330^\circ=-\sin30^\circ$ ($330^\circ$ is in the fourth quadrant at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal.) So $\sin330^\circ=-\frac12$.
\textbf{d } $\sin420^\circ=+\sin60^\circ$ (on second revolution). So $\sin420^\circ=\frac{\sqrt3}2$.
transcription.notes: Exact text and mathematics visually checked against original asset.

transcription.tex:
\textbf{e } $\sin(-300^\circ)=+\sin60^\circ$ ($-300^\circ$ is in the first quadrant at $60^\circ$ to the horizontal.) So $\sin(-300^\circ)=\frac{\sqrt3}2$.
\textbf{f } $\cos120^\circ=-\cos60^\circ$ ($120^\circ$ is in the second quadrant at $60^\circ$ to the horizontal.) So $\cos120^\circ=-\frac12$.
\textbf{g } $\cos300^\circ=+\cos60^\circ$ ($300^\circ$ is in the fourth quadrant at $60^\circ$ to the horizontal.) So $\cos300^\circ=\frac12$.
transcription.notes: Exact text and mathematics visually checked against original asset.

transcription.tex: \textbf{h } $\cos225^\circ=-\cos45^\circ$ ($225^\circ$ is in the third quadrant at $45^\circ$ to the horizontal.) So $\cos225^\circ=-\frac{\sqrt2}2$.
transcription.notes: Exact text and mathematics visually checked against original asset.

transcription.tex:
\textbf{i } $\cos(-210^\circ)=-\cos30^\circ$ ($-210^\circ$ is in the second quadrant at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal.) So $\cos(-210^\circ)=-\frac{\sqrt3}2$.
\textbf{j } $\cos495^\circ=-\cos45^\circ$ ($495^\circ$ is in the second quadrant at $45^\circ$ to the horizontal.) So $\cos495^\circ=-\frac{\sqrt2}2$.
\textbf{k } $\tan135^\circ=-\tan45^\circ$ ($135^\circ$ is in the second quadrant at $45^\circ$ to the horizontal.) So $\tan135^\circ=-1$.
\textbf{l } $\tan(-225^\circ)=-\tan45^\circ$ ($-225^\circ$ is in the second quadrant at $45^\circ$ to the horizontal.) So $\tan(-225^\circ)=-1$.
transcription.notes: Exact text and mathematics visually checked against original asset.

transcription.tex:
\textbf{m } $\tan210^\circ=+\tan30^\circ$ ($210^\circ$ is in the third quadrant at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal.) So $\tan210^\circ=\frac{\sqrt3}3$.
\textbf{n } $\tan300^\circ=-\tan60^\circ$ ($300^\circ$ is in the fourth quadrant at $60^\circ$ to the horizontal.) So $\tan300^\circ=-\sqrt3$.
\textbf{o } $\tan(-120^\circ)=+\tan60^\circ$ ($-120^\circ$ is in the third quadrant at $60^\circ$ to the horizontal.) So $\tan(-120^\circ)=\sqrt3$.

\textbf{4} Solve for $0\le x\le180^\circ$ the equations:
\textbf{a} $\sin(x+20^\circ)=\frac12$.
\textbf{b} $\cos2x=-0.8$, giving your answers to 1 decimal place.
transcription.notes: Exact source wording, working and annotations visually checked; source mistakes retained.

transcription.tex:
\textbf{a} Let $X=x+20^\circ$. So $\sin X=\frac12$. As $X=x+20^\circ$, then as $0\le x\le180^\circ$, so $0+20\le x\le180^\circ+20$. So the interval for $X$ is $20^\circ\le X\le200^\circ$.
$X=30^\circ,150^\circ$, i.e. $x+20^\circ=30^\circ,150^\circ$. So $x=10^\circ,130^\circ$.
transcription.notes: Exact source wording, working and annotations visually checked; source mistakes retained.

transcription.tex:
\textbf{b} Let $X=2x$. So $\cos X=-0.8$. As $X=2x$, then as $0\le x\le180^\circ$, so $2\times0\le X\le2\times180^\circ$. So the interval for $X$ is $0\le X\le360^\circ$.
$X=143.13^\circ,216.87^\circ$, i.e. $2x=143.13^\circ,216.87^\circ$. So $x=71.6^\circ,108.4^\circ$.
transcription.notes: Exact source wording, working and annotations visually checked; source mistakes retained.
